brief: GS's Mark Wilson argues equity upside into year-end is increasingly clear, built on two market impulses. Meta's Muse product broke out Monday, accelerating AI's consumer-adoption timeline and sparking FOMO, while 10yr yields extended a 7-month rise (the longest in 50 years), driven by strong US PMI data rather than capex competition or energy inflation. Two consensus views hold that bond-driven equity risk is growing and that Gulf de-escalation plus safe passage past the Midterms are required before re-risking. Wilson counters with three reasons. On inflation, tariff pass-through is waning, prior hikes are biting, and Iran's negotiating window (open until Nov 2) plus Muse's deflationary effect on consumer goods point to downside energy-price risk. On growth, fiscal tailwinds (per Jan Hatzius) fade, gas and mortgage costs bite consumers, AI capex slows, so central banks likely disappoint on hikes versus current pricing. On earnings, Snider's team flags record 'other income' as unreliable and memory/semis stocks as over-earning, but expects core earnings to stay strong through 2027. Since the data doesn't support stagflation, Wilson expects the historic Midterms-to-year-end equity rally, extending to Europe and the UK as the energy-price threat recedes.
